summary: The note previews the inaugural "Maplewood Mile," a neighborhood fun run on September 15, 2023 in the Maplewood district that combines fitness, community fair festivities, and fundraising. Organized by local health enthusiasts, it offers multiple distances, themed route features, training groups, safety measures, and local business sponsorship. Proceeds support local initiatives like the Green Spaces project and the Maplewood Community Center's after-school programs.
one_line: The inaugural Maplewood Mile fun run on September 15, 2023 blends fitness, community fair fun, and fundraising for local Maplewood causes.
key_facts: The inaugural "Maplewood Mile" neighborhood fun run takes place on September 15, 2023 in the Maplewood district.
The event was spearheaded by local health enthusiasts including Mark Henderson and Jenna Willis.
Mark Henderson has been a resident coach for the past five years; Jenna Willis is a nutritionist by profession.
Funds raised support the Green Spaces project and the Maplewood Community Center's after-school programs.
Participants can choose a 10-kilometer race or a 2.5-kilometer family fun run.
Local businesses will operate hydration and snack stations, and local musicians and DJs will perform along the route.
The route includes themes ranging from bubble zones to heritage stops, where local historians narrate neighborhood history.
Free weekly "Couch to 5K" training groups for beginners are led by volunteer runners, including Henderson, before the race.
After the finish line, a community fair offers a farmer's market, kids' craft stations, free health checks, and yoga sessions.
A pasta dinner at Maplewood Community Center on the eve of the race serves as a carb-load and social mixer with keynote speakers.
Safety measures include volunteer marshals at every turn, local police oversight, a risk assessment, and an emergency plan.
Sponsors, including tech startups and family-run restaurants, donated T-shirts, water bottles, post-race meal vouchers, and lucky draw prizes.
The event promotes itself with a dedicated website, interactive map, countdown clock, Spotify playlist, and the hashtag #MaplewoodMile2023.
Lydia Schmidt, a long-time event organizer, helped shape the event strategy.
